title: Sync: Lifecycle & Customer Spotlight — Weekly SE + ProServices Notes (2029-08-28)
summary: Weekly sync focused on three active integrations (LumenPay, Cartwright Systems, HearthAI). Main themes: capacity gating for Dedicated, KV-cache warmup causing tail latency, and A/B rollout health for model variant gating.
body:
Meeting date: 2029-08-28
Attendees: Maya Chen (owner), Liam O'Connor, Priya Desai, Carlos Mendez, Sophie Tan, Anil Rao (SRE consult), customer reps on ad-hoc calls
Duration: 45m

TL;DR:
- LumenPay: Dedicated capacity reserve approved, provisioning ETA 2029-09-03; final network peering window set for 09/05; risk: initial KV-cache cold start causing intermittent 95th pct latency spikes.
- Cartwright Systems: A/B rollout at 2% to validate quantized gpt-small-8bit; observed slight degradation on numeric extraction evals -> rollback plan ready.
- HearthAI: Data residency checklist signed; private deployment staging images failing sanity checks due to missing KMS integration in staging.
- Cross-customer: SRE flagged a pod OOM trend on shared autoscale group when prefix cache rehydration triggers burst. Action to add memory headroom and telemetry.

Agenda:
1) Quick round-robin customer updates (10m)
2) Technical deep-dive: KV cache warmup patterns and mitigations (15m)
3) Capacity and networking: Dedicated pool provisioning and peering windows (10m)
4) Risks, action items, owners (10m)

Customer spotlight: LumenPay (payments fintech)- Status: Onramp in final validation. Dedicated capacity order approved (monthly committed GPUs). Provisioning request created by infra (PR linked in artifacts).- Recent findings: During load tests we see 95th percentile latency jump from 220ms -> 680ms for cold prefixes when KV cache is empty and batch coalescing bundling increases token fan-out. The effect is amplified when sequence length >512.- Root cause hypotheses: (1) Cache warmup causes extra memory churn and small GC pauses in tensor allocator, (2) Autoscaler spin-up latency aligning with first heavy requests.- Mitigation underway: Pre-warm KV cache using synthetic requests (SE script: prewarm-kv-loom), add 10% memory headroom on GPU serving pool, and adjust autoscale cooldown to 90s.- Next milestone: Network peering scheduled 2029-09-05; post-provision smoke test on 09/06.- Open actions:
  - Carlos to run prewarm script in staging and report RPS profile by 2029-08-30.
  - Anil to add memory headroom change and open infra rollout ticket (PROSERV-9821) by 2029-08-29.

Customer spotlight: Cartwright Systems (SaaS catalog search)- Status: Early production A/B test of quantized model gpt-small-8bit as lower-cost fallback. 2% traffic routed via feature flag.- Findings: Automated QA on structured extraction (invoice parsing) shows mean F1 drop of 3.7% for the quantized variant. Latency improves ~28% median.- Decision: Pause rollout to 0% if quality degrades further beyond 4% F1. We have rollback automation ready (SE-7743).- Technical notes: Investigating bitpacking alignment differences between the quantized runtime and the reference CPU eval harness that explain softmax noise at tail tokens.- Open actions:
  - Priya to coordinate with Applied ML to reproduce numeric extraction mismatch in a reproducible eval harness by 2029-08-31.
  - Sophie to hold rollback drills with the customer and validate traffic cutover time < 30s by 2029-09-02.

Customer spotlight: HearthAI (healthcare insights)- Status: Private deployment pipeline in staging; compliance artifacts approved except KMS staging key integration.- Issue: Staging deploys fail post-init because KMS plugin in the private control plane is not loading for the staging tenancy. This blocks end-to-end verification of full-disk encryption and audit logs.- Impact: Delays customer sign-off for on-prem launch; timeline risk if KMS fix slips past next week's window.- Open actions:
  - Liam to triage KMS init logs and escalate to security infra by 2029-08-29 with specific repro steps and heap traces.
  - Maya to draft a conditional plan to run a limited-scope E2E with mocked KMS (audit caveat) to validate functionality by 2029-09-04.

Cross-cutting technical discussion: KV-cache warmup and serving ergonomics- Observed pattern: Several customers see tail latency correlated with cache rehydration events (restarts, scale events, or fresh deployments).- Short-term mitigations discussed:
  1) Controlled prewarm (synthetic prefix requests published as part of rollout pipeline).
  2) Gradual traffic ramp plans to avoid large fan-out on first live requests.
  3) Increase memory pool overhead and slightly lengthen autoscale cooldown to avoid oscillation.- Long-term ideas:
  - Instrumentation: Add a KV-cache warmup telemetry dimension (cache_hits_during_warmup, avg_kv_latency) into Console dashboards.
  - Runtime: Explore async background prefetch worker that runs at low priority during scaled-down windows.

Capacity & networking notes- Dedicated pool provisioning: Procurement confirmed GPUs available week of 09/02; infra to schedule reclamation and migration windows.- Peering: Customers prefer evening maintenance window (US-PST 10pm-12am). Confirmed for LumenPay. Cartwright requested weekend window — Sophie to negotiate.

Risks and escalations- SRE alert trend: Pod OOMs on autoscale group when multiple cold prefix requests arrive simultaneously — likely memory allocation spike from cache population and batch coalescing. Severity: P2.- Mitigation: Immediate memory headroom + rollout of prewarm hooks. If incidents continue, we will gate new deployments for affected customers and open a hotfix branch to throttle prewarm concurrency.

Action items (owner — due)
- Carlos Mendez — run KV prewarm in staging for LumenPay and share logs (2029-08-30)
- Anil Rao (SRE) — implement memory headroom change and create infra ticket (PROSERV-9821) (2029-08-29)
- Priya Desai — reproduce extraction F1 drop in eval harness and share minimal repro (2029-08-31)
- Sophie Tan — validate rollback automation and schedule weekend peering window talk with Cartwright (2029-09-02)
- Liam O'Connor — triage KMS init failure and escalate to security infra (2029-08-29)
- Maya Chen — prepare conditional mock-KMS E2E plan and customer communication draft (2029-09-04)

Notes to archive:
- Keep prewarm scripts under se/playbooks/prewarm and add runbook steps to onramp checklist.
- Add a short blurb to Console notes about ongoing tail-latency investigations so CS teams can set expectations.

Next sync: 2029-09-04 — focus: post-provision LumenPay smoke test, Cartwright A/B decision, HearthAI KMS resolution.
